texts.preamble: Annapoornavanitha Canteen vs The Superintendent on 6 November, 2016 Author: Devan Ramachandran Bench: Devan Ramachandran In The High Court Of Keralaat Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice Devan Ramachandran Wednesday, The 23Rd Day Of August 2017/1St Bhadra, 1939 WP(C).No. 39634 of 2016 (D) ---------------------------- Petitioner : ----------------- Annapoornavanitha Canteen (A Unit Of Nedumangad Municipality, Kudumbasree Cds-Ii), Nmc 13/1666-1, Nedumangad Taluk District Hospital Compound, Nedumangad, Thiruvananthapuram, Represented By Its Conveneor S.Syamalakumari. By Advs.Sri.Anil Kumar M.Sivaraman Smt.M.Shahina Respondents : ------------------------- 1. The Superintendent Nedumangad Taluk District Hospital, Nedumangad P.O., Thiruvananthapuram, Pin-695541. 2. Hospital Management Committee Nedumangad Taluk District Hospital, Nedumangad, Pin-695541, Represented By Secretary/Convenor. *Addl.R3 Impleaded Addl.R3.
texts.facts: The petitioner is stated to be an unregistered association of women, who calls themselves the 'Annapoorna Vanitha Canteen', which they say is a unit of the Kudumbasree CDS attached to the Nedumangad Municipality. According to them, they were running a canteen in the Nedumangad Taluk District Hospital, which is now called the District Hospital, for the last more than 18 years and their complaint is that their services were terminated by the Superintendent of the said Hospital, the 1st respondent herein, W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017 without notice to them and therefore, that it is illegal. They, on such allegation, pray in W.P.(C).No.39634 of 2016 that they be permitted by the 1st respondent to run the canteen without interruption. As regards W.P.(C).No.25257 of 2017 is concerned, the claim of the petitioner is that an amount of 3,71,000/- is due to them from the Hospital and they pray that this amount be returned to them by the Annapoornavanitha Canteen vs The Superintendent on 6 November, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14406999/ 3 respondents, without delay. 4. The pleadings on record would show that the petitioner's assertion is that they have been running a canteen in the Hospital for the last more than 18 years.
texts.arguments: However, the petitioner has not been able to present on record any document to show how they were allowed to operate this canteen uninterruptedly and without specific contracts being entered into for the last 18 years. I can only visualise such situation because it being a Kudumbasree Unit, the petitioner was allowed to run the canteen of the Hospital without a proper tender and without calling for other competitors for the several years past. This, in my view, cannot give the petitioner a vested right to maintain that they should be allowed to run the canteen for all years to come. According to the 1st respondent, the petitioner was only paying 3,000/- per month and therefore, that the grant of tender in favour the aforementioned Ms.Aswathy for an amount of 77,000/-, has obtained to the Hospital a profit of 74,000/- per month. The petitioner cannot maintain that they should be allowed to run the canteen without a tender and that, no competitors can be allowed because they have been operating for the last 18 years without interruption. As regards the claim of the petitioner, in W.P.(C).No.25257 of 2017, that an amount of 3,71,000/- is due to them is concerned, I see that this claim is based on Ext.P1 statement of account made by the them before the 1st respondent under the "Mother and Child Free Food Scheme". The learned counsel for the petitioner submits W.P.(C).Nos.39634 of 2016 & 25257 of 2017 that the claim of the petitioner has, in fact, been admitted by the 1st respondent, as is evidenced by Ext.P4 information obtained by them. However, the learned Senior Government Pleader submits that in Ext.P4 there is no admission as to the amounts due to the petitioner.
